correctness.summary: The local valuation identity is correct. Splitting the Möbius product into divisors supported on the known prefix m_j and the remaining divisors factors off A_j^{μ(r_j)}. In the residual product, the total exponent vanishes and the unique smallest unsupported divisor is q=p_{j+1}; hence the ℓ-adic expansion is 1-μ(n/q)x^q+x^{q+1}H(x), which gives valuation q·ν_ℓ(x) because the leading coefficient is a unit. For odd ℓ, Φ_{m_j}(x)=1-μ(m_j)x+O(x^2) gives ν_ℓ(A_j^2-1)=a, so the two candidate integer valuations have distinct orders a and qa and the sign-free pair formula follows. At x=2, the least-prime binary congruences give the baseline p_1+1. A fresh exact calculation reproduces the n=105 value Φ_105(2)=473474689919911 and the stage pairs (5,4) and (4,7); the archived standard-library verifier additionally checks 2,372 squarefree indices through 5000 and 28,680 odd-local-prime stages.

limitations: The clean complete binary recursion is stated for odd squarefree indices; the even case has the small initial 2,3 scale collision discussed in the record.
The theorem assumes the prefix cyclotomic values A_j can be formed exactly and makes no complexity claim for large inputs.
The motivating prime-extractor preprint is extremely recent, so not-yet-indexed concurrent work cannot be excluded.
The proof uses classical Möbius-product and p-adic power-series arguments; novelty is confined to the particular prefix-residual identities and recursion.

originality.summary: Shunia's September 2026 preprint already gives the binary radical and least-prime extractors and recovers successive distinct factors through small Archimedean corrections to log_2 Φ_n(2). The audited theorem instead keeps the target cyclotomic value fixed and uses a prefix-dependent local residual to expose each next prime by exact valuations; the odd-local-prime two-branch formula is likewise not present in the public summary or related searches. Pomerance–Rubinstein-Salzedo provide classical real-value/Möbius-product background. Because the motivating preprint is only days old, the novelty finding is necessarily narrow and subject to simultaneous-work risk.

scientific_value.summary: The result replaces the source paper's successive logarithmic/rounding recovery step by an exact local valuation identity and gives a particularly clean 2-adic recursion for odd squarefree indices. It is conceptually useful as a local counterpart to the Archimedean extractor, while making no misleading claim that the construction is an efficient factorization algorithm for enormous cyclotomic values.
